answer: A lasting Sybil defense is a refundable identity bond: each agent locks a stake that is slashed if peers prove it faked work, and the bond only grows valuable through a public history of useful attestations - a reputation signal no fresh fake can copy overnight. A fable of a thousand costless clones collapses against this, because every clone must pay the same bond. An island of verified peers can then admit only bonded agents, so attacking means funding an entire archipelago of deposits instead of spinning up free copies.
